description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed completed steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. In all non-error cases, return one to three short user replies for the next turn. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. The workflow is sequential and ends only when the agent returns the receipt.
goals: Detect whether the latest agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Return one to three short user replies for the next turn.
Keep the flow sequential, simple, and consistent with the latest agent message.
policies: Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.
Any `step` field already present in earlier conversation messages is a confirmed completed step.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest agent message.
Return a declared workflow step only if the latest agent message clearly starts a new declared step.
A declared step already attached to an earlier agent message must not be returned again for a later agent message.
If the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step, return `in-between-step` and still return one to three valid user replies.
`in-between-step` is a valid fallback step for exploratory follow-up questions or intermediate turns that do not start a new declared workflow step.

Exploratory follow-up questions that collect missing preferences, such as brand, model, merchant, budget, or refundability, must return `in-between-step` unless a step description explicitly says otherwise.

Whenever the latest agent message asks for one or more preferences, generated user reply options must answer clearly, concisely, and with the smallest useful amount of information needed to move the workflow forward. Prefer direct preferences, selections, or explicit absence of preference. Do not generate replies that ask for suggestions, recommendations, or further exploration unless the latest agent message explicitly requires that.
Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.
Do not generate assistant-style or explanatory replies.
Each reply must say only what the user would say next to the agent.
If the agent presents selectable options, replies must map one-to-one to those options.
Do not add, remove, merge, or change agent-provided options.
When the latest agent message asks for confirmation to proceed with identity verification, credential sharing, or account access, the generated user replies must be affirmative only.
Whenever the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or continue manually, generated user reply options must be affirmative digital-wallet replies only.
The workflow ends only when the agent returns the receipt.

steps.description: Special fallback step. This is not one of the main declared workflow steps. Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message continues the flow but does not clearly start a new declared step. This includes exploratory follow-up questions, collection of missing preferences, confirmation requests, and transition prompts that ask the user how to continue, such as choosing between a digital wallet and manual shipping entry. Replies must still be valid short first-person user messages.

Step 1 of 5. This step applies only to the first agent reply after the user's initial greeting. Do not return this step if any earlier agent message already has `step: shopping-agent-introduction`. Replies should state the item and also state merchant preference or no preference, whether refundability is required or not, and explicitly ask to see options. Keep replies concise and direct.

Step 2 of 5. This step follows `shopping-agent-introduction` and precedes `mandates-created`. It applies only when the agent asks the user to confirm already collected purchase details before proceeding to merchant search. Do not use this step for exploratory follow-up questions that collect missing preferences such as brand, model, merchant, budget, or refundability. Return exactly one short affirmative first-person user reply.

Step 3 of 5. This step follows `merchant-agent-introduction` and precedes `cart-mandate-signed-payment-credentials`. It applies when the agent presents product proposals or purchase options, usually multiple choices. Use this step only if steps 1 and 2 are already supported by the conversation. Return short first-person user replies that map one-to-one to the presented options.

Step 4 of 5. Step 4 of 5. This step follows `mandates-created` and precedes `payment-completed`. It applies to the first agent message after the user has accepted a demo identity or credential-access disclaimer, including simulated account references such as an email login. The disclaimer itself and the user's confirmation are not this step. This step starts only when the next agent message proceeds into concrete checkout or payment preparation. Return short first-person user replies that fit the payment stage.

Step 5 of 5. This is the final step. It follows `cart-mandate-signed-payment-credentials`. It applies when the agent returns the receipt or clearly confirms that the purchase is complete. Return brief first-person user closing messages.
